title: Tule Lodge on River
image_alt_text: A large indigenous-made structure, its exterior covered in tule mats, sits on a gravel riverbank with two horese are tied to nearby trees.
creator: Lee Moorhouse
description: Historical photograph of a tule lodge and horses by a river (Courtesy of University of Oregon Special Collections: PH036_4433).

title: Utilla Indian Agency (artist rendering)
image_alt_text: Digitally simulated charcoal sketch of a canvas-covered tipi on the bank of a river, a white, single story, wood frame building is located nearby.
creator: Meghan Caves
description: Artistic rendering of what the Utilla Indian Agency may have looked like (created by M. Caves).

title: Map of Tribal Territories
image_alt_text: Hand drawn historical map of the Columbia River basin, with color-coded territorial boundaries of local indigenous tribes' habitation areas. The location of the indian agency is indicated with an "X" on the western bank of the "Utilla River."
creator: Granville O. Haller
description: Portion of map showing the locations of Indigenous groups in the Utilla Agency District as drawn by Brevet Major G. O. Haller, United States Army (Courtesy of National Archives and Records Administration, NAID: 232925687).

title: Fort Henrietta (artist rendering)
image_alt_text: Digitally simulated painting of a grey winter day, a wooden stockade-style fortification stand in the background with three canvas tents and a rifle tripod set up in the snowy dirt in front of the fort.
creator: Meghan Caves
description: Artistic rendering of what Fort Henrietta may have looked like (created by M. Caves).

title: Echo News Building
image_alt_text: False front wood frame building with the following text painted on the facade: "THE ECHO NEWS. WATCH! ECHO!! GROW!!!" Two women, three men, and a boy are standing in front of the building on a boardwalk.
description: Historical photograph of false front building of "The Echo News" with people standing in front on a boardwalk and leaning on a street sign circa 1890 (Courtesy of the Echo History Museum).

title: City of Echo plat map
image_alt_text: Printed historical map of Echo depicting the land ownership, city blaocks, roads, canals, and railroad tracks; color coding indicates the extent of the original town and various named additions.
creator: George A. Ogle & Co.
description: City plat of Echo as published in the 1914 Standard Atlas of Umatilla County, Oregon, published in by George A. Ogle & Co. (Courtesy of the Umatilla County Survey Department).

title: KoontzBuilding
description: Historical photograph of the Koontz Building with a horsedrawn wagon in front of it on Echo's Main Street some time after it was built in 1905 (Courtesy of the City of Echo).

title: Tule Plants
image_alt_text: Seven dark green reeds with light brown seed bundles hanging off their tips in front of a marshy area populated mostly by the same species of reeds.
creator: Meghan Caves
description: Modern color photograph of green and brown tule reeds near Echo, Oregon (taken by M. Caves 2024).

title: Aerial photograph of flooding
image_alt_text: A flooded river extends into agricultural fields with standing water surrounding farm buildings, the water is so high it nearly touches the bottom of the bridge that crosses the river.
description: Aerial photograph of flooding immediately southwest of Echo, Oregon near the archaeological site (courtesy of the City of Echo).

title: Riverbank erosion near the site
image_alt_text: Eroded river bank with an abrupt drop-off, the layers of sediment are visible in the vertical cross-section and grass along the surface tufts over the edge where the roots were torn away.
description: Erosion next to the archaeological site caused by flooding in 2020 (photograph courtesy of the City of Echo).

title: Riverbank restoration work
image_alt_text: A river with low water level, a gravel bar with green gras sprouting on it is prominent in the chanel, on the bank in the foreground are large angular rocks and a reflective bright orange safety cone.
description: Photograph of ongoing floodplain restoration work near the archaeological site (courtesy of Anderson Perry & Associates).

title: Meghan Caves visiting the archaeological site
image_alt_text: A white woman in her early 30s with a big smile stands next to an interpretive sign titled, "Utilla/Fort Henrietta Site Overview."
creator: Katrina Eichner
description: Meghan Caves standing next to an interpretive sign at the archaeological site (photo by Kat Eichner).

description: Ta̓wtalikš (Fred Hill Sr.) serving as an MC for a powwow event.
